title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook 6 Comprehensive 2026
author: Elena Morales
content:
Overview

This playbook captures Redwood Inference’s standard process for on-call rotations, incident triage, runbooks, postmortems, game days, and external communications (status page and customer templates). It is intended to be the single source of truth for responders and stakeholders during operational events.

Objectives
- Restore customer-facing functionality as quickly and safely as possible.
- Minimize blast radius and data exposure.
- Communicate clearly and repeatedly to internal stakeholders and customers.
- Capture a timestamped record for post-incident analysis and continuous improvement.

Scope and ownership
- Primary owners: Eng SRE (oncall scheduling, tooling, escalation) and Eng Platform (runbook authorship).
- Services covered: inference-gateway, model-router, runtime-workers, kv-cache, embed-indexer, console-api.
- Exceptions: security incidents with data exposure are owned jointly with Security & Compliance and follow the security incident process (see security-and-compliance incident-response).

Key SLAs & SLOs (summary)
| Service | Primary Pager | P99 latency SLO | Error-rate SLO (5m) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| inference-gateway | pagerduty:inference-gw | 200ms | <0.5% | External edge; highest customer impact |
| model-router | pagerduty:model-router | 300ms | <1.0% | Routes to variants |
| runtime-workers | pagerduty:runtime | - | <2.0% | Throughput/backpressure sensitive |

On-call rotations and responsibilities
1) Roles and coverage
   - Primary on-call (1): First responder for pages tied to pagerduty services. Expected response time: 5 minutes for P1 pages.
   - Secondary (backup): Takes over if primary is unavailable or incident escalates.
   - Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates cross-team response for P1/P0 incidents. Usually a senior SRE or Eng Platform lead.
   - Communications Lead: Drafts status updates and customer-facing communications.
   - Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Service owners called for deep debugging.

2) Rotation cadence
   - Team-level rotations: 1 week on-call per person, 4-week schedule for each SRE pod.
   - Pager duty shifts start Monday 08:00 UTC and end following Monday 08:00 UTC.
   - On-call handoff: Each shift must run a 15-minute handoff via the #oncall-handoff channel with updates in the rotation calendar. Document ongoing incidents, alerts suppressed, and planned deploys.

Paging & escalation matrix
- Severity classification (quick guide):
  - P0: System-wide outage or data loss impacting >50% customers. Immediate page, escalate to IC, cross-org bridge.
  - P1: Major degradation (costly latency/error or single customer outage for >10% of traffic). Page primary, notify secondary within 10 min if unresolved.
  - P2: Partial degradation or degradation with a known mitigation. Track in ticket; page only if auto-alert triggers.
  - P3: Informational/SLI drift — create ticket for scheduled work.

- Escalation steps (automated + manual):
  1. PagerDuty page -> Primary on-call. If no ack in 5 min, PD escalates to Secondary.
  2. If 15 minutes with no resolution for P0/P1, escalate to Eng SRE lead and open an incident bridge.
  3. If the incident impacts customers or requires cross-team coordination, IC is assigned and the Communications Lead drafts the first status update.

Incident triage checklist (first 15 minutes)
- Confirm the alert: check Grafana dashboards, recent deploys, and PagerDuty payload.
- Identify blast radius: which services, regions, customers affected?
- Capture initial timeline and create an incident tracker (choose either JIRA incident template or the lightweight incident doc: incident-YYYYMMDD-service).
- Is there a quick mitigation? (e.g., rollback, scale up, circuit-breaker). If yes, apply with approval from IC or Primary on-call.
- Communicate: post an initial internal update in #incidents and set an incident severity.

Runbook template (canonical, use per-service)
- Title: <service-name> runbook
- Pager: <pagerduty-service>
- Oncall-owner: <team/name>
- Symptoms: list of alerts/log patterns that map to the runbook
- Impact: expected customer impact and SLOs affected
- Quick checks (commands/queries):
  - kubectl get pods -n production | grep <service>
  - kubectl logs -n production <pod> -c <container> --since=10m
  - curl -v https://gateway.prod.redwood.example/healthz
  - /opt/redwood/bin/diag --service model-router --last 30m
- Common mitigations (ordered):
  1. Increase replica count: kubectl scale deploy/<service> --replicas=<n>
  2. Restart failing pods: kubectl rollout restart deploy/<service>
  3. Temporarily route traffic to a compatible model-variant via model-router: curl -X POST ...
  4. Rollback last deploy: kubectl rollout undo deploy/<service> --to-revision=<rev>
- Rollback criteria: increased error-rate > 2x baseline and no improvement in 10 minutes after mitigation.
- Post-action checks: SLO dashboards, logs for exceptions, memory/CPU utilization.
- Owner & runbook last updated date.

Example service runbook excerpt: inference-gateway
- Symptoms: 502/504 spikes in edge logs; p99 latency > 350ms; connection refused to runtime-workers.
- Quick checks:
  - Edge errors: kubectl logs -n edge deploy/inference-gateway --since=5m | grep "502" | wc -l
  - Runtime pods: kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep runtime-worker
  - Network errors: sudo tc qdisc show dev eth0  (on gateway host)
- Mitigations: scale replicas, enable degraded-mode routing (route 10% traffic to canary fallback), open runtime-workers autoscaling buffer.

Incident commander responsibilities
- Declare the incident severity and objectives (safety, stability, communications).
- Maintain the incident timeline and delegate tasks.
- Approve major mitigation steps (rollbacks, traffic shutdowns).
- Sign off on when a postmortem is required.

Communications (internal & customer)
- Internal updates cadence: every 15 min for P0/P1 until the incident is stabilized, then every 30-60 min.
- Use the incident Slack channel (#incident-<id>) and pin the incident tracker link.
- Status Page updates: Communications Lead publishes to status.redwood.example when customer impact is confirmed.

Internal status update template (Slack)
- [INC-<id>] Severity: P1 — inference-gateway degraded
- Impact: 20% of requests returning 502s globally since 11:02 UTC
- Mitigation: scaled runtime-workers to 10 -> 30 replicas; traffic routing adjusted to fallback variant.
- Next update: 13:15 UTC or on significant change.

Public status page update template
- Title: Degraded performance for inference API (partial outage)
- Time: 2026-02-19 11:05 UTC
- Summary: We are seeing increased errors and latency for the Inference API. A subset of customers may experience failed requests and slow responses.
- Impact: 10-30% requests may fail or be delayed.
- Current status: Investigating. Engineering is actively working on mitigation.
- Next update: in 30 minutes.

Customer email template (for targeted customers)
- Subject: Incident affecting Redwood Inference API — [INVESTIGATING]
- Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  We are currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood Inference API that may impact requests for your workspace. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. We will follow up with an update in 30 minutes or sooner as we have new information.
  Impact: Some requests may fail or be delayed.
  Workaround: If you can temporarily route critical traffic to a pinned model-variant or lower QPS, this will reduce errors.
  We apologize for the disruption and will provide a root cause and next steps after resolution.
  — Redwood Support & SRE

Postmortem process and template
- Trigger: Any P0 or P1 incident requires a postmortem published within 72 hours. P2 incidents require a postmortem if there was manual mitigation or customer impact.
- Timeline: Draft due in 48 hours; final published within 7 days after action owners close agreed items.
- Postmortem template (fillable):
  - Title: Incident INC-<id> — <short description>
  - Severity: P0/P1/P2
  - Timeline: ordered timestamps (ISO) with short events (alert -> ack -> mitigation -> recovery -> close)
  - Impact: customer-facing impact, SLO breach details, customers affected by org id if applicable
  - Root cause: short summary and contributing factors
  - Detection: how it was detected (alert, customer report)
  - Mitigations: actions taken during incident and their effectiveness
  - Long-term fix / action items: owner (email), ETA, status
  - Learnings: what changed in runbooks/alerts/oncall after the incident
  - Attachments: relevant logs, dashboard links, PRs, rollback refs

Example timeline excerpt:
- 2026-02-19T11:02:13Z — Alert: inference-gateway 502 spike (>5% 1m)
- 2026-02-19T11:06:40Z — Primary on-call acknowledged and started triage
- 2026-02-19T11:12:05Z — Escalated to IC; bridge opened; scaled runtime-workers
- 2026-02-19T11:28:03Z — Error-rate dropped to 1.2%; further stabilization ongoing
- 2026-02-19T12:05:50Z — Service considered recovered; monitoring in observation mode

Action tracking and follow-up
- Use a Jira board labeled incident-postmortems for tracking action items. Each action must have an owner and ETA. Owners must update progress weekly until resolved.
- Example actions: tweak alert thresholds, improve observability for KV cache misses, add automated failover for model-router.

Game days & training
- Frequency: quarterly squad-level game days + annual company-wide incident simulation.
- Goals: validate runbooks, exercise communication paths, measure mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to mitigate (MTTM).
- Standard scenario example: simulated runtime-workers OOM during peak traffic; expected outcomes: scale policies engage, traffic re-routing activates, IC coordination and status page update within 15 minutes.

Monitoring and observability guidance
- Dashboards: SLO-overview, error-heatmap, region-latency, runtime-pod-health.
- Alerts: prefer rate-based alerts (5m, 1m) tuned to SLOs and avoid noisy per-instance alerts.
- Logs & traces: include request-id and customer-id in logs for fast correlation. Ensure KV cache log level and eviction metrics are emitted.

Runbook hygiene and ownership
- Every service must have a living runbook stored in the confluence runbooks folder and referenced from the service README.
- Runbook owners are responsible for monthly reviews and after any incident or deploy that touches the service.

Appendices
- Tools & links:
  - PagerDuty configuration: https://pagerduty.redwood.example/service/inference-gw
  - Incident templates: /confluence/eng-platform/incident-review-templates-2025
  - Status page editor: https://status.redwood.example/admin
  - Runbook location: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks

- Quick checklist for declaring a major incident (IC checklist):
  1. Confirm P0/P1 and create incident tracker.
  2. Open a conference bridge (Zoom / Meet) and invite IC + SMEs.
  3. Post initial internal summary and create an external status draft.
  4. Assign Communications Lead and start customer notification draft if applicable.
  5. Track and assign action items in Jira.
